page.layout: One page of text, one column, running head at top, page number at top left. Marginal catchword in italics at the start of the second paragraph, left margin. Catchword "æter-" at lower right.

main_text.l: & spiritualis illa vita Christiani militis. Vita, in-
quit Apostolus, quam vivo, vivo per fidem Filii
Dei, Galat.2.20. Ecce vivimus beneficio fidei. &
Eph.3.17. Christus inhabitat in cordibus nostris
per fidem. Christus autem vita nostra est. Quare
per fidem vita illa spiritualis & obtinetur, & con-
servatur: qua si denudatum fuerit cor nostrum,
de vita spirituali actum est. Galea militis mun-
dani una est, caput undequaq; muniens, neque
partibus suis distincta: sic quoque galea militis
Christiani una est tota, non distincta partibus,
quam spem salutis nominat Apostol9 [?]. Ergo spes
est quæ munit ac protegit spiritualem sensum
atque motū; qua sublata nullus est amplius sen-
sus atq; motus spiritualis. Hic habes illa tria quæ
non uno in loco commendata sunt ab Apostolo,
fidem, charitatem, spem; quę si retineantur, con-
servatur salus Christiani hominis, conservantur
spiritualis vita, spiritualis sensus atque motus.
De hac armatura lege Esa.59.17. lege quoque de
panoplia, h.e. de universa armatura Christiani
militis, Eph.6.17. quo loco fides non thoraci, sed
scuto, comparatur, quo omnia jacula mali illius
ignita extinguuntur; sed in re nihil interest, sive
scuto, sive thoraci fides comparetur.
Salutis illius de qua dixit
proxime, hoc & sequenti versu duo substernit
fundamenta, quibus ipsa nititur: quæ quidem
doctrina eo pertinet ut salutis spes fit certa ac indu-
bitata. Primum salutis fundamentum, est Dei decre-
tum æternum, sive prædestinatio nostri ad vitā
æter-

page.notes: Page number "182" is printed top left. Running head is "In Epist. Pauli", set in small capitals. The italic phrase at the start of the second paragraph is a marginal note on the left, set in the indent. The superscript after "Apostol" is read as 9, with [?] marked on the word. The catchword "æter-" is printed at the lower right. Long s is transcribed as s throughout, including "Esa.59.17." where the scan shows an f-like form. Some letters near the right edge are cropped by the page edge (for example "vitā"). The black ink on the right edge and the small mark below the text are not printed text and are not transcribed.
